title: Store an explicit file start time in the wtap header
description:
Some file types, like BLF and LOG3GPP, have an explicit capture start
time in their header which is distinct from "the time stamp of the first
packet or other record with a time stamp." Store that in the wtap struct
similarly to how per-file encapsulation and timestamp precision is
stored. Use it for those two file formats.

For each record, the relative time to the capture start exists if and
only if the record has a time stamp, and the a capture start time
exists. Rather than having each record store the relative time to the
capture start (and whether it's valid), calculate it from the capture
start time for each record that has a time stamp similar to how relative
times to the first record or time reference frame are calculated.

We could possibly get rid of the value in the packet_info struct as well
and have the Plot dialog use the frame data function too.

Ping #20691, #20699

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • dab2834a - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • 88e6cf70 - Store an explicit file start time in the wtap header
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21333/diffs?diff_id=1490463121&start_sha=8dac87730b3aa2d3d76ffd6d46293dea87c5a632)
Possibly a better long term approach is to store this in the SHB, and to amend the pcapng specification for a start time option in the SHB.

This sounds like an excellent idea!

We could also try `isb_starttime` and `isb_endtime` until a SHB solution exists:

* When writing pcapng: Write the same value to each interface.
* When reading back pcapng: Check if all interfaces have this option. If yes, use the smallest of all values.

Right, ISBs are another option. When writing pcapng, we might want to write an ISB with just a start time immediately after the IDB, and then write the ordinary ISB later. That would work better with streaming, piping, etc.

Discussion for all this is spread across a lot of different bugs and MRs, my apologies.
How does this affect !21337?  It seems like it can solve the problem for BLF, the main reason !21337 was created.

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21337 was created to fix the Capture File Properties Dialog. This MR here does not do that. However, there might be merging conflict that requires rebasing.
added this merge request to the [merge train](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_trains) at position 2
We should also cherry-pick this into 4.6, since the bug fix of the Capture File Properties Dialog depends on it: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21337
